content.content: deccy's verbs share one substrate with five seams: dispatch of argv to verbs, file-backed node reads, jj driven as a subprocess, one output and refusal envelope, and whole-operation markers. Verbs own their behavior and output lines; the substrate owns crossing process, file, and repo boundaries and nothing else.
content.rationale: Every verb crosses the same process, file, and repo boundaries; without a shared substrate each verb would re-decide those crossings and drift. The single binary makes the shared process boundary real and the jj repo makes file and repo crossings shared. Scoping the substrate to boundary-crossing only keeps future verbs from re-litigating boundaries while leaving verb behavior to the verbs.
